b.v: About 30 minutes. This course is a real project: by the end you have a working app online and a link to put on your CV.

1) How it fits together

day-3.t: Step 3 — The Task model and the admin

b.v: Today's goal

v: Store tasks in the database
Link each task to its owner
Check it in the admin

b.v: About 25 minutes.

@Python
# tasks/models.py
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import models

class Task(models.Model):
    owner = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="tasks")
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    done = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    due = models.DateField(null=True, blank=True)
    created = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ["done", "due", "-created"]

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title

Check it.|Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/ and sign in.|Create a second user, for example sara.|Add two tasks for yourself and one for sara.|You will use these to prove that users only see their own tasks.

1) What you get

v: GET /api/tasks/ = my tasks (add ?status=done or ?status=active)
POST /api/tasks/ = add a task
PATCH /api/tasks/5/ = change part of task 5, e.g. done
DELETE /api/tasks/5/ = delete task 5
POST /api/token/ = send username and password, get a token

b.v: Filtering by owner in get_queryset is what keeps users apart. Without it, anyone signed in could read or delete everyone's tasks by changing the number in the address.
While signed in to the admin, open http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/tasks/ – DRF shows a page where you can try the API.

day-5.t: Step 5 — Sign-in tokens and testing the API

b.v: Today's goal

v: Get a token for a user
Call the API the way React will
Prove one user cannot see another's tasks

b.v: About 25 minutes.
React cannot use the admin's login cookie, so it signs in once, gets a token and sends it with every request in the Authorization header.

@Terminal
# get a token (use your own username and password)
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/token/ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"username\": \"ali\", \"password\": \"your-password\"}"
# answer: {"token":"9944b09199c62bcf9418ad846dd0e4bbdfc6ee4b"}

# list tasks with the token
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/tasks/ -H "Authorization: Token 9944b09199c62bcf9418ad846dd0e4bbdfc6ee4b"

# add a task
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/tasks/ -H "Authorization: Token 9944b0..." -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"title\": \"Buy milk\"}"

# no token = refused
curl -i http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/tasks/

v: 201 = created
204 = deleted, no content
400 = your data was wrong (the answer says which field)
401 = not signed in / bad token
404 = not found – also what you get for someone else's task

b.v: The safety test – do it now.|Get a token for sara.|With sara's token, ask for one of your task ids: /api/tasks/<your id>/|You must get 404. If you get the task, go back to Step 4 and check get_queryset.
A token is like a password. Never post it in screenshots, on GitHub or in chats.

day-9.t: Step 9 — Python power-ups: import tool and tests

b.v: Today's goal

v: Write a Django command in Python that imports tasks from a CSV file

Run the tests before every change

b.v: About 35 minutes.
1) Import tasks from a spreadsheet

@Python
# tasks/management/commands/import_tasks.py
# (create the folders management/ and management/commands/, each with an empty __init__.py)
import csv
from datetime import date
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand, CommandError
from tasks.models import Task

class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = "Import tasks from a CSV file with columns: title,due (due as YYYY-MM-DD, optional)"

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        parser.add_argument("csv_file")
        parser.add_argument("--user", required=True)

    def handle(self, csv_file, user, **options):
        try:
            owner = get_user_model().objects.get(username=user)
        except get_user_model().DoesNotExist:
            raise CommandError(f"No user called {user}")
        made = skipped = 0
        with open(csv_file, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for row in csv.DictReader(f):
                title = (row.get("title") or "").strip()
                if len(title) < 2:
                    skipped += 1
                    continue
                due = row.get("due") or None
                Task.objects.create(owner=owner, title=title, due=date.fromisoformat(due) if due else None)
                made += 1
        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS(f"Imported {made} tasks, skipped {skipped}."))

2) Tests that prove the app is safe

@Python
# tasks/tests.py
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from rest_framework.test import APITestCase
from .models import Task

User = get_user_model()

class TaskApiTests(APITestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.ali = User.objects.create_user("ali", password="pass-12345")
        self.sara = User.objects.create_user("sara", password="pass-12345")

    def test_must_sign_in(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.client.get("/api/tasks/").status_code, 401)

    def test_create_sets_owner(self):
        self.client.force_authenticate(self.ali)
        r = self.client.post("/api/tasks/", {"title": "Buy milk"}, format="json")
        self.assertEqual(r.status_code, 201)
        self.assertEqual(Task.objects.get(id=r.json()["id"]).owner, self.ali)

    def test_cannot_see_other_users_tasks(self):
        theirs = Task.objects.create(owner=self.sara, title="Sara's task")
        self.client.force_authenticate(self.ali)
        self.assertEqual(self.client.get("/api/tasks/").json(), [])
        self.assertEqual(self.client.get(f"/api/tasks/{theirs.id}/").status_code, 404)
        self.assertEqual(self.client.delete(f"/api/tasks/{theirs.id}/").status_code, 404)

    def test_title_too_short(self):
        self.client.force_authenticate(self.ali)
        r = self.client.post("/api/tasks/", {"title": "x"}, format="json")
        self.assertEqual(r.status_code, 400)

@Terminal
python manage.py test
All four tests must say OK. Run them every time you change the back end – they catch mistakes before your users do.

# /etc/systemd/system/taskboard.service
[Unit]
Description=Task Board API
After=network.target

[Service]
User=www-data
WorkingDirectory=/var/www/taskboard/backend
EnvironmentFile=/etc/taskboard.env
ExecStart=/var/www/taskboard/backend/venv/bin/gunicorn config.wsgi --bind 127.0.0.1:8000 --workers 3
Restart=always

[Install]

DJANGO_SECRET_KEY=paste-a-long-random-value-here
